Voaters, what was one of your proudest moments?

When I was about 10 years old, I was on a cruise (lucky me) and there was a a dodgeball game going on on the deck. I decided i'd "play", which consisted of me hiding behind other people to avoid the dodgeballs. My strategy worked, because the after a while the only people left were me, one guy on my team, and one guy on the other team. From my 10 year old eyes, the guy on the other side was a lot bigger than i'd want to deal with, so I continued to kind of run from the balls. This went on for maybe 10 minutes, with the other guy on my team trying to hit the other, and failing. All the previous eliminated people were watching from the side, and one called out. "Just pick up a ball!" I thought why not? and picked up one and just threw it at him. I assume what happened is the other guy didn't expect me to do anything, but I hit him square in the chest. Maybe not my proudest moment, but back then it probably was.

I was in psychology class, and I hadn't heard of the Milgram experiment. Loved the professor, loved the class, was very interested in it. One day, my professor told us that we'd be doing an experiment. He lined out what it would be like and the gist was, people would answer questions, and wrong answers would get stronger shocks. You couldn't quit, if you volunteered-- but you would have to volunteer. People could volunteer to be questioner or answerer, but they had to finish whatever they started.

I had a problem with this and found it odd. I started asking questions. I started asking so many questions that my professor got annoyed and he started threatening me with getting sent to the principal's office. I zoned out and debated whether I was overreacting and paranoid or should report him. I hadn't really reached a conclusion but was leaning toward the latter when he got my attention and delivered his explanation.

I felt just shocked and at a loss at first, but later, I came to feel pretty proud about it. There was another similar instance involving hazing to join a group, and I didn't think the process was ethical, so I refused it. In both cases, I was congratulated by the person I trusted. In both cases... I was the only one speaking up. Not the only person with questions, not the only person who thought something was wrong, but the only person who actually spoke up.

Since then, I've gotten in the habit of analyzing things that make me feel uncomfortable, and speaking up when I think something is wrong. It's always helped me feel okay with myself at the end of the day, that I can say I feel I have integrity. I always feel good now, whenever I'm reminded that I won't be bought by something, or intimidated in that way. It made all the difference to have no fucking clue I was being tested, because I'd always wonder what I'd be like, 'in the dark'. Now, at least for these types of things, and the others that have come up in my life, I don't have to wonder.

You have a strong moral compas and the integrity to don't abandon those principles, that's really something to be proud of! It's not easy being the only one who stands up for what's right, especially in the face of "authority". I've experienced some difficult moral decisions, but I'm also proud to say that when I look in the mirror I know that I've handled every situation as best as I could and always stuck by what was "right".

It's definitely something I've automatically programmed into my thinking overall, which is good. I don't get so surprised when something sketchy pops up, and I don't have to think as long about what I should do.

Your approach no doubt saves you a lot of grief and guilt. Good for you and the people around you!
